knowledge:
- key_parameters: positionName=The column name in the input data frame representing genomic positions when calling createArrayData ;; quiet=A logical parameter in geneToSNPList (defaulting to TRUE) that suppresses warnings when finding overlaps between genes and study SNPs
- alternatives: GLOSSI vs VEGAS. Use GLOSSI when analyzing independent SNPs (e.g., after LD-pruning). Use VEGAS when analyzing correlated SNPs, as it utilizes a correlation/linkage disequilibrium (LD) matrix to simulate the null distribution and account for correlation structure.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have SNP-level p-values from a genome-wide association study (GWAS) and want to aggregate them to test the association of specific gene sets or biological pathways with a phenotype.
- pitfalls: Mapping gene IDs to SNPs is highly sensitive to genome builds; users must ensure that the gene transcripts database (e.g., TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene) matches the coordinate build of the SNP positions. GLOSSI assumes independent SNPs; running it on highly correlated SNPs without prior LD-pruning will violate statistical assumptions and yield incorrect p-values. Setting quiet=TRUE in geneToSNPList may suppress valid warnings about coordinate mismatches.

workflows.name: glossi_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform gene set analysis on independent (LD-pruned) SNP p-values using the GLOSSI method.
input: arrayData.csv (GWAS results containing SNP IDs, p-values, chromosomes, and genomic positions)
workflows.stages:
1. Convert GWAS data frame to a GRanges object using createArrayData.
2. Map gene IDs in the GeneSetCollection to SNP IDs using geneToSNPList and a transcript database.
3. Subset the GWAS GRanges to independent SNPs and extract named p-values.
4. Run GLOSSI using glossi.
5. Extract results using pValue, degreesOfFreedom, and statistic.
6. Visualize results using plotPvals.
workflows.code:
arrayDataGR <- createArrayData(geneSetAnalysis[["arrayData"]], 
    positionName="Position")
geneSets <- geneSetAnalysis[["geneSets"]]
library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene)
txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene
genesHg19 <- genes(txdb)
snpsGSC <- geneToSNPList(geneSets, arrayDataGR, genesHg19)
indep <- geneSetAnalysis[["indepSNPs"]]
pvals <- arrayDataGR$P[is.element(arrayDataGR$SNP, indep$V1)]
names(pvals) <- arrayDataGR$SNP[is.element(arrayDataGR$SNP, indep$V1)]
gRes <- glossi(pvals, snpsGSC)
pValue(gRes)
degreesOfFreedom(gRes)
statistic(gRes)
plotPvals(gRes, main="GLOSSI P-values")

workflows.name: vegas_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform gene set analysis on correlated SNP p-values using the VEGAS method, accounting for linkage disequilibrium (LD).
input: arrayData.csv (GWAS results containing SNP IDs, p-values, chromosomes, and genomic positions)
ld_matrix.rds (Square, symmetric matrix of correlation/LD values among SNPs)
workflows.stages:
1. Convert GWAS data frame to a GRanges object using createArrayData.
2. Map gene IDs in the GeneSetCollection to SNP IDs using geneToSNPList and a transcript database.
3. Run VEGAS using vegas with the mapped GeneSetCollection, SNP GRanges, and LD matrix.
4. Extract results using pValue, degreesOfFreedom, and statistic.
workflows.code:
arrayDataGR <- createArrayData(geneSetAnalysis[["arrayData"]], 
    positionName="Position")
geneSets <- geneSetAnalysis[["geneSets"]]
library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene)
txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene
genesHg19 <- genes(txdb)
snpsGSC <- geneToSNPList(geneSets, arrayDataGR, genesHg19)
ldMat <- geneSetAnalysis[["ldMat"]]
vRes <- vegas(snpsGSC[1], arrayDataGR, ldMat)
pValue(vRes)
degreesOfFreedom(vRes)
statistic(vRes)
